The chips row feels more natural to me — the labels sit right there in a line and I just tap "Recipes" to narrow things down. Selecting it dropped the list to just the two recipe cards and the count updated to 2 results, with the search box still sitting there ready. The sidebar worked identically, but for the handful of labels I'd have, the row across the top feels lighter and more at-a-glance. So let's go with the chips.

Seeing the label right on each card is good — that's how I'd know at a glance what something is filed under. Filtering the moment I pick one, the count updating, and search still being available all match what I wanted. Recipes, Work, Travel, and Home are perfectly reasonable samples to try it with.

Two things I want to make sure are part of how labels work, since they matter to how I'd actually use this: these should be my own labels that I make up as I go, not a fixed set — my real life isn't just those four. And a single bookmark should be able to carry more than one label, because plenty of things belong in two places at once. Can you confirm labels work that way when we get into creating them?

This filtering behavior itself is good.
